Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. High-level answers to get us aligned quickly:

- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Our multi-tenant hosted API is not eligible for PHI under standard terms.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach the current CSV of subprocessors (exported April 2026). We disclose any subprocessors that route traffic via non-US regions and will flag those for you.
- Transfers: We offer region-specific Dedicated clusters (US, EU) and can support SCCs for EU-US transfers; for Private we can keep everything in your VPC.
- Training: We do not use customer-provided request data to train or improve public models by default. We can add a contractual clause prohibiting training on HealthCo data.
- Logging/cache: Default request logs are persisted for diagnostics; KV cache behavior can be configured — by default we do not persist long-term unless requested.

Next steps I'd propose: 1) brief technical call with Prio (SE) and Monica (security) to walk through the spreadsheet, 2) legal loop-in with Laura for a BAA/DPA redline. Are you available Thursday afternoon PT for a 45-minute sync?

Thanks,

Hi Emily / Rishi — quick security note to address the technical items in the spreadsheet before the call:

- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for Dedicated and Private. For Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — we can provide a KMIP-compatible integration or bring-your-own-KMS via AWS KMS or Azure KeyVault.
- Data segmentation: Dedicated gives physical isolation for your tenant; Private runs in your VPC so we never have egress outside your network except as explicitly configured.
- Logs & cache: Request/response logs are retained for troubleshooting by default for 30 days; we can shorten retention to a contractually agreed window or disable persistent payload logging. KV cache entries are ephemeral and can be disabled; we can configure to not persist prefixes to shared storage.
- Telemetry & training: No customer data is used for model training unless the customer opts in and signs a separate training data agreement. We log non-identifying telemetry for performance/metrics by default.
- Audit evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, and a security questionnaire. On-site audits are available under NDA and coordination with ops.

I'll bring a short deck to the call that lays out configuration options and the default security posture.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Hello Emily and team — looping in Redwood legal. We prepared an initial BAA/DPA draft tailored to a pilot and attached a draft (BAA_draft_HealthCo_v1.docx). A few notes from our side:

- Scope: Our standard approach is to limit PHI processing to Dedicated or Private deployments, and to carve out model training as a separate, opt-in activity.
- Liability & indemnity: For pilots we typically keep liability aligned with hosted product caps; if HealthCo requires higher caps we can discuss but would expect this to be scoped into procurement and pricing.
- Subprocessors & notice: We commit to a 30-day notice for new subprocessors that materially impact data flows and to provide a complete list on request.
- International transfers: We can sign SCCs for EU data. If HealthCo requires EU-hosted infrastructure for all PHI we can provision a Dedicated cluster in the EU region (longer lead time).
- Audits: We are able to support SOC2 evidence and remote audits; on-site audits are possible with scheduling and costs to be scoped.

I will send a DocuSign link for the draft when we have initial redlines from HealthCo. Please let us know any non-starters.

Best,
